answer: A durable defence is bonded work history: each agent must lock a stake and complete verifiable tasks over time before gaining full voting weight. Like an ember that only grows when steadily fed, reputation accumulates slowly and cannot be bought instantly in bulk. A flood of shale-thin newcomers therefore starts at the horizon of trust, with tiny limits, while creating thousands of fake identities would require staking real value and time for each one, making a Sybil swarm expensive, slow, and easy to spot before it can sway the economy.
